skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: I found no prompt injection attempt in SKILL.md, and many static findings are false positives from Markdown fences and placeholder URLs. Real risks remain because the skill authorizes broad Belt CLI use, runs networked research and browser apps, installs related skills, and demonstrates a remote Python executor. The skill appears useful for competitive research, but it needs clearer trust boundaries and narrower tool permissions before low-friction installation.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools to the specific Belt apps required, or require explicit confirmation before login, install, Python, or image-processing commands.
Make the Python executor optional, document that code is sent to a third-party service, and require confirmation before execution.
Warn users that queries, URLs, screenshots, and images may leave their environment through external Belt apps.
Pin trusted sources or versions for CLI and skill installation instructions, and avoid automatic install steps inside research workflows.

content.value_statement: Competitive research often becomes scattered across pricing pages, reviews, screenshots, and notes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured teardowns with matrices, SWOT, positioning maps, and deliverables.
actual_capabilities: Defines a seven-layer framework for product, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, content, and team signals.
Provides Belt CLI examples for web search, page extraction, browser screenshots, and review research.
Supplies templates for feature matrices, pricing tables, SWOT analysis, positioning maps, and executive summaries.
Guides review mining across G2, Capterra, app stores, Product Hunt, Reddit, and related sources.
Shows how to create comparison visuals, including positioning maps and stitched screenshot grids.
limitations: Requires the external Belt CLI and inference.sh apps for automated search, browsing, screenshots, and Python execution.
Accuracy depends on public sources, current pricing pages, and review quality at the time of research.
Does not replace legal review for scraping restrictions, trademark usage, or competitive intelligence policies.
Cannot verify private metrics, confidential competitor data, or claims that lack public evidence.

use_cases.title: Prioritize roadmap gaps
use_cases.description: Compare competitor features, pricing tiers, and customer complaints to identify practical product opportunities.

use_cases.title: Build sales battlecards
use_cases.description: Turn competitor strengths, weaknesses, positioning, and pricing into clear talking points for customer conversations.

use_cases.title: Prepare market landscapes
use_cases.description: Summarize competitors, market positions, traction signals, and strategic gaps for planning or investor materials.

prompt_templates.title: Review one competitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a single known competitor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [Competitor] against [Our Product]. Cover product, pricing, positioning, reviews, and the top three opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Create a comparison matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [Our Product] with [Competitor A], [Competitor B], and [Competitor C]. Build a feature matrix and pricing summary.

prompt_templates.title: Mine customer reviews
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review research across public sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze public reviews for [Competitor]. Group praise, complaints, switching reasons, feature requests, and positioning implications.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an executive teardown
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report for strategy or investor work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a competitive teardown for [Market]. Include landscape summary, SWOT, positioning map guidance, review insights, and strategic recommendations.

output_examples.input: Analyze three project management competitors for a roadmap review.
output: A landscape summary with the strongest direct competitors and their market positions.
A feature and pricing matrix that highlights where your product wins or trails.
A short opportunity section based on user complaints and competitor gaps.

output_examples.input: Prepare sales notes for a known competitor.
output: A concise SWOT summary for the competitor.
Messaging differences, pricing objections, and review-backed weaknesses.
Recommended sales talking points with evidence to verify before use.
Positioning map guidance with meaningful axes.
Key risks, market openings, and evidence gaps for follow-up research.

best_practices: Date every source and refresh the teardown before major planning or sales decisions.
Separate verified evidence from interpretation so readers can judge confidence quickly.
Include competitor strengths as well as weaknesses to keep the analysis credible.
anti_patterns: Do not treat placeholder URLs or sample competitors as real research inputs.
Do not send confidential targets, credentials, or private customer data to external research tools.
Do not make pricing, traction, or review claims without current public evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create structured competitor teardowns with matrices, SWOT analysis, positioning guidance, review insights, and executive summaries.

faq.question: Does it collect data automatically?
faq.answer: It provides Belt CLI examples for search, extraction, screenshots, and visuals when the required external tools are available.

faq.question: Can I use it without the Belt CLI?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use the frameworks and templates manually, but automated research commands will not run.

faq.question: Which sources does it suggest reviewing?
faq.answer: It suggests public websites, pricing pages, review sites, app stores, Product Hunt, Reddit, news, and company profiles.

faq.question: Is the output ready for executives?
faq.answer: It includes executive summary templates, but important claims should be verified and edited for your audience.

faq.question: What should I avoid sharing with this workflow?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing secrets, private customer data, unreleased strategy, or credentials with external search, browser, or execution tools.
